subject: Private deployment: request for network & control/data-plane review

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment: request for network & control/data-plane review

Hi Joe / Nora —

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. As discussed, Acme is piloting a private deployment of Redwood (control plane hosted in our dedicated region, data plane inside your VPC) for the staging environment. Before we lock the pilot timeline, we need a short design review with your network/security team focused on control-plane reachability, egress policies, and diagram alignment.

High-level summary of what we think the deployment will look like:
- Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane endpoints in us-west-2 (private endpoints + mutual TLS); no inbound public traffic to customer VMs.
- Data plane: Customer-owned VPC (staging) running inference workers; Redwood runtime connects outbound to control plane over TLS.
- Connectivity options we discussed: VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink depending on routing and CIDR overlap.
- Egress: customer to manage internet egress; we recommend a minimal set of outbound IPs and ports for telemetry and model pulls.

Ask: could you share a reference diagram (subnets, NAT/proxy placement, route tables) and any gating requirements from your security team (approved egress ranges, required firewall rules, PKI requirements for mTLS)?

If you can send a diagram and a short list of must-have controls, we’ll annotate with the Redwood control/data-plane responsibilities and propose a short technical session (30-60 min) to finalize.

Appreciate it — we want to make sure the staging rollout has a clean handoff so the Dedicated pilot can go live on the timeline.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Joe Sanchez <joe.sanchez@acme.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Lim <nora@enterprise-hub.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T07:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: request for network & control/data-plane review

Monica —

Thanks, we sketched a first-pass diagram and a short security requirements doc and attached both (acme_vpc_diagram_v1.png; acme_security_requirements.pdf). A few quick notes up front:
- Our staging VPC uses a single /20 split across public, private-app, and data subnets.
- We currently funnel outbound traffic through an outbound proxy (proxy.company:3128) behind a NAT for egress auditing; any external TLS must be allowed via proxy.
- We prefer to use TGW for shared services; peering likely to cause overlap issues with our prod ranges.
- For mTLS, we can accept server certs signed by Redwood's CA but need a CSR process for client certs for our jump hosts.

Suggested next step: technical session with our infra/security folks on Wednesday or Thursday next week. Are you available?

Joe
Joe Sanchez

Subject: Re: Private deployment: request for network & control/data-plane review

Thanks for the diagram and notes, Joe — good context. Sharing a few internal asks/clarifications so we can finalize the architecture before the call. I attached our Redwood Private VPC checklist for reference.

Questions / comments (high level):
1) Control plane reachability
   - Confirming: Redwood control plane will be in us-west-2; we will provide a small set of outbound FQDNs and IP ranges for mTLS endpoints. Does your proxy allow explicit FQDN allowlists or only IP-based egress?
2) Auth and PKI
   - We support mutual TLS. For client certs issued to Acme jump hosts or proxies, we need a documented CSR flow and cert rotation window (recommend 90d).
3) Network topology preferences
   - We prefer Transit Gateway for connectivity to avoid CIDR overlap complications. If TGW is not feasible, please list conflicting CIDRs and we can evaluate NAT + port-forwarding options.
4) KV/cache and data locality
   - For low-latency KV/cache warm-ups, we recommend colocating the worker subnets with the model artifact storage (S3-compatible endpoint) in the same AZs. If your staging uses cross-AZ access, estimate added tail latency.
5) Egress & telemetry
   - We will emit telemetry/usage pings to endpoints that require allowing outbound TLS (443). If your policy forces proxying, Redwood telemetry can be proxied but we need to confirm connection timeout and retry behavior.

Proposed agenda for the technical session (30-60 min):
- Roll through the diagram and map responsibilities (5 min)
- Networking deep-dive: routes, TGW vs peering, NAT/proxy placement (20 min)
- Security: mTLS CSR flow, cert rotation, audit logs (15 min)
- Rollout cutover checklist and timeline (10 min)

I attached: redwood_handbook_private_vpc_checklist.pdf (short checklist we use for pilots).

Would Wednesday 2026-11-24 at 11:00 PT work for the ACME and Redwood infra teams? If not, propose two slots.

Thanks,
Sergio
Director, Customer Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_handbook_private_vpc_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
